prog-bbm-023.question: What is the principle underlying Closed Loop Stimulation (CLS) rate response in Biotronik pacemakers?
options: Intracardiac ventricular impedance during each contraction
Minute ventilation, derived from respiratory transthoracic impedance
Endocardial acceleration measured at the tip of a dedicated lead
An accelerometer in the can, sensitive to chest wall movement
commentaires: Correct: CLS measures unipolar RV tip-to-can impedance during each contraction, reflecting contractility.
Incorrect: minute ventilation is the Boston Scientific rate response sensor.
Incorrect: endocardial acceleration is the MicroPort SonR signal, used to optimise CRT.
Incorrect: Biotronik devices also have an accelerometer, but as a separate sensor; CLS uses it only to identify rest.
prog-bbm-023.explication: CLS measures unipolar intracardiac impedance between the tip of the ventricular lead and the can during each contraction. Changes in this impedance curve reflect myocardial contractility (inotropy), which is controlled by the same autonomic nervous system as the sinus node. Rate response therefore reacts not only to physical activity but also to mental stress, which sets it apart from motion sensors. It works with standard leads and initialises automatically. Biotronik devices also have an accelerometer (R modes), but as a separate sensor; CLS uses it only to identify periods of rest. Minute ventilation (Boston Scientific) and endocardial acceleration (MicroPort SonR) are different signals.
prog-bbm-023.aRetenir: CLS = intracardiac ventricular impedance, reflecting contractility, responding to both physical and mental stress.

prog-bbm-024.question: A 52-year-old woman has recurrent, frequent reflex syncope causing injury, with a cardioinhibitory response on tilt testing (asystole > 3 s). Pacing is decided upon. Which programming is supported by the randomised SPAIN trial?
options: VVI at 40 bpm with rate hysteresis
DDD with Rate Drop Response
DDD with Closed Loop Stimulation (DDD-CLS)
AAI(R) with accelerometer-based rate response
commentaires: Incorrect: VVI loses AV synchrony and does not respond early to the phase preceding syncope.
Incorrect: Medtronic Rate Drop Response was evaluated in the double-blind VPS II trial, with no significant reduction in syncope.
Correct: in SPAIN, 72% of patients in DDD-CLS had at least a 50% reduction in syncope, versus 28% in placebo mode.
Incorrect: AAI is ineffective against the cardioinhibitory component, which often involves paroxysmal AV block.
prog-bbm-024.explication: SPAIN was a double-blind crossover trial in patients aged 40 years or older with highly recurrent vasovagal syncope and a cardioinhibitory response on tilt testing. It compared DDD-CLS pacing with a placebo DDI mode at 30 bpm. The proportion of patients with at least a 50% reduction in syncope was 72% with DDD-CLS versus 28% in placebo mode. The presumed advantage of CLS is that it detects the increase in contractility preceding the vasodepressor phase and raises the pacing rate before the heart rate falls. Medtronic Rate Drop Response showed no significant benefit under double-blind conditions (VPS II). VVI is unsuitable (loss of AV synchrony, no early response), and AAI is ineffective against the cardioinhibitory component.
prog-bbm-024.aRetenir: Selected cardioinhibitory reflex syncope: DDD-CLS (SPAIN trial).

prog-bbm-025.question: How does the CLS algorithm build its resting reference to detect an increase in demand?
options: A single curve recorded during initialisation at implant
Monthly manual calibration with an exercise test in clinic
The mean sinus rate over the last 24 hours, taken as rest
The average of the last 256 resting curves, paced and sensed kept apart
commentaires: Incorrect: a curve frozen since implant would not track changes in the patient; the reference is updated continuously.
Incorrect: CLS initialises and adapts automatically, without exercise-test calibration.
Incorrect: CLS is not anchored to the sinus rate but to resting impedance curves.
Correct: the resting reference averages the last 256 curves recorded at rest (identified by the accelerometer), separately for Vp and Vs.
prog-bbm-025.explication: Biotronik's CLS practical guide describes three steps: building the resting curves, comparing them with the curve of the current cycle (load curve), then automatic adaptations. The resting reference curves are continuously updated from the last 256 curves recorded at rest, rest being identified by the accelerometer. They are kept separate for paced and sensed ventricular events. The difference between the current-cycle curve and the reference is converted into a pacing rate. No manual exercise-test calibration is needed, and a curve frozen since implant would not track changes in the patient.
prog-bbm-025.aRetenir: CLS compares each impedance curve with a continuously updated resting reference (256 curves, paced and sensed kept separate).

prog-bbm-026.question: What does the Vp Suppression feature of a Biotronik dual-chamber pacemaker do when intrinsic AV conduction is present?
options: Switches to AAI(R) with a VVI backup running at a reduced rate
Switches from DDD(R) to ADI(R) to avoid unnecessary ventricular pacing
Shortens the AV delay as soon as an intrinsic QRS occurs, to maintain V pacing
Extends the AV delay (positive AV hysteresis) to allow conduction through
commentaires: Incorrect: AAI(R) with a reduced-rate VVI backup is Boston Scientific RYTHMIQ.
Correct: when conduction is present, Vp Suppression switches from DDD(R) to ADI(R); the ventricle is only monitored.
Incorrect: shortening the AV delay to maintain V pacing is negative AV hysteresis, useful in CRT; the effect is the opposite.
Incorrect: positive AV hysteresis is IRSplus, the other Biotronik option; Vp Suppression changes mode.
prog-bbm-026.explication: Vp Suppression is Biotronik's algorithm for minimising ventricular pacing. When intrinsic conduction is present, the device switches from DDD(R) to ADI(R): the atrium is paced or sensed and the ventricle is only monitored. If conduction deteriorates, it returns to DDD(R) to provide ventricular pacing. The principle is similar to Boston Scientific RYTHMIQ or MicroPort SafeR, but the switching criteria are specific to each manufacturer. IRSplus, the other Biotronik option, remains in DDD and extends the AV delay (positive hysteresis). Shortening the AV delay would have the opposite effect, increasing RV pacing.
prog-bbm-026.aRetenir: Vp Suppression = DDD(R) → ADI(R) switch as long as intrinsic AV conduction is present.

prog-bbm-027.question: In a Biotronik pacemaker from the Edora family, what are the standard settings of the Vp Suppression parameters?
options: Return to DDD if 2 of the last 4 A-A cycles have no Vs, no other setting
On by default at implant, with no programmable parameters
ADI after 6 consecutive Vs; return to DDD if 3 of 8 cycles lack conduction
ADI after 12 consecutive Vs; return to DDD after 2 consecutive blocked P waves
commentaires: Incorrect: 2 of 4 A-A cycles without ventricular sensing is the Medtronic MVP switching criterion.
Incorrect: Vp Suppression is Off as standard, and two parameters are programmable once it is enabled.
Correct: pacing suppression after 6 consecutive Vs (1 to 8), pacing resumed if 3 of 8 cycles lack conduction (1 to 4).
Incorrect: 12 intrinsic R waves and 2 consecutive blocked P waves are MicroPort SafeR criteria.
prog-bbm-027.explication: In the Edora 8 technical manual, Vp Suppression is Off as standard. Once enabled, two parameters govern it: pacing suppression after x consecutive Vs (1 to 8, standard 6) and pacing resumption after x of 8 cycles (1 to 4, standard 3). In other words, ventricular pacing is abandoned once conduction has been confirmed over 6 cycles, then resumed if 3 of 8 cycles show loss of conduction. The criteria "2 consecutive blocked P waves" and "12 intrinsic R waves" belong to MicroPort SafeR, and "2 of 4 cycles" to Medtronic MVP. Keeping these algorithms apart is essential to interpret a Holter or a stored EGM correctly.
prog-bbm-027.aRetenir: Vp Suppression (Edora standard): ADI after 6 consecutive Vs, return to DDD if 3 of 8 cycles lack conduction.

prog-bbm-028.question: What is the purpose of the IRSplus (Intrinsic Rhythm Support) feature in Biotronik devices?
options: Promoting intrinsic AV conduction through positive AV hysteresis
Shortening the AV delay to maintain biventricular pacing
Supporting the intrinsic rhythm by lowering the basic rate at night
Switching to ADI(R) as soon as intrinsic AV conduction is confirmed
commentaires: Correct: IRSplus extends the AV delay (positive hysteresis) to allow intrinsic conduction to emerge.
Incorrect: shortening the AV delay for CRT is negative AV hysteresis, the opposite of IRSplus.
Incorrect: despite its name, IRSplus does not act on the basic rate; a night-time reduction is the job of a night rate function.
Incorrect: switching to ADI(R) is Vp Suppression, the other Biotronik algorithm for minimising RV pacing.
prog-bbm-028.explication: IRSplus is a positive AV hysteresis option designed to allow intrinsic conduction to emerge by extending the AV delay. It is an alternative to Vp Suppression (which switches to ADI(R)) for minimising RV pacing in patients with preserved or intermittent conduction. The 2019 ICD consensus update in fact mentions it in its Biotronik implementation ("DDD, consider IRS Plus"). Conversely, negative AV hysteresis is used in CRT to maintain ventricular pacing. Despite its name (Intrinsic Rhythm Support), it does not act on the basic rate. A very long AV delay may, however, promote poorly tolerated AV dyssynchrony, which should be watched for in patients with a very long PR interval.
prog-bbm-028.aRetenir: IRSplus = positive AV hysteresis to promote intrinsic conduction.

prog-bbm-029.question: In a Biotronik device, the Capture Control (Active Capture Control) parameter offers the settings ON, OFF and ATM. What does ATM stand for?
options: Atrial Tachycardia Management: ATP for atrial tachycardias
Automatic Threshold Monitoring: threshold measured and trended, amplitude unchanged
Auto Threshold Margin: amplitude = measured threshold plus a safety margin
Auto-Test Magnet: threshold test triggered by applying a magnet
commentaires: Incorrect: Capture Control is a threshold function, unrelated to the treatment of atrial tachycardias.
Correct: in ATM mode, the threshold is measured and trended without changing the programmed amplitude.
Incorrect: adapting the amplitude to the threshold plus a margin is ON mode, not ATM.
Incorrect: a magnet triggers a threshold test in some devices, but that is not what ATM means.
prog-bbm-029.explication: Capture Control automatically measures the pacing threshold in each chamber with a lead. In ON mode, it adapts the amplitude to the measured threshold plus a programmable safety margin; in ATM mode (monitoring only), it simply measures and trends the threshold, without changing the programmed amplitude. This mode is useful when a fixed amplitude is preferred (recently implanted lead, doubts about measurement reliability) while still tracking threshold changes, particularly on remote monitoring. For the LV in CRT, Capture Control is also available with threshold tracking or ATM.
prog-bbm-029.aRetenir: Capture Control: ON = measurement + amplitude adaptation; ATM = measurement and trending only.

prog-bbm-030.question: In the SMART Detection algorithm of Biotronik dual-chamber ICDs, what is the decision when the averaged ventricular rate is faster than the atrial rate?
options: R-R stability and A/V ratio analysed before any decision
Onset criterion and PR stability analysed before any decision
QRS morphology compared with the reference before any decision
VT counter incremented with no further test; VT therapy delivered
commentaires: Incorrect: R-R stability and the A/V ratio are tested when the atrium is faster than the ventricle.
Incorrect: onset and PP and PR stability are used in the decision trees for a 1:1 ratio.
Incorrect: morphology comparison is MorphMatch, which cannot be enabled together with SMART.
Correct: V faster than A indicates a ventricular origin; the VT counter is incremented without further testing.
prog-bbm-030.explication: SMART Detection continuously compares atrial and ventricular intervals, each averaged over 4 intervals. If the ventricular rate exceeds the atrial rate, the ICD increments the VT counter without further testing: dissociation with V faster than A indicates a ventricular origin. If A is faster than V, a supraventricular origin is presumed, with exceptions tested by R-R stability and the A/V ratio. With a 1:1 ratio, specific decision trees use the onset criterion and PP and PR stability. SMART applies only to the VT1 and VT2 zones, never to the VF zone.
prog-bbm-030.aRetenir: SMART: V > A = VT with no further test; discrimination applies only in VT zones.

prog-bbm-031.question: Regarding the SMART Detection and MorphMatch discriminators of Biotronik ICDs, which statements are correct?
options: SMART Detection and MorphMatch cannot be enabled at the same time
SMART Detection is mainly intended for single-chamber detection, MorphMatch being the method of choice in multi-chamber devices
MorphMatch can withhold therapy in the VF zone if the morphology matches
MorphMatch requires a functioning atrial lead
commentaires: Correct: the Rivacor manual states that either MorphMatch or SMART Detection is programmed, never both.
Incorrect: it is the other way round: SMART relies on the A/V relationship and suits multi-chamber devices; MorphMatch is mainly used in single-chamber devices.
Incorrect: like the other discriminators, MorphMatch acts only in VT zones, never in the VF zone.
Incorrect: MorphMatch analyses the ventricular signal alone and does not require an atrial lead.
prog-bbm-031.explication: The Rivacor manual states that either MorphMatch or SMART Detection is programmed, never both. MorphMatch compares the QRS morphology of the tachycardia with a reference of conducted rhythm; it is mainly used for single-chamber detection (notably VR-T DX) but remains available in multi-chamber devices. SMART, which relies on the relationship between atrium and ventricle, is the method of choice in dual-chamber devices and CRT-Ds. Like the other discriminators, MorphMatch does not act in the VF zone. It does not require an atrial lead, since it analyses the ventricular signal alone. The Biotronik implementation of the 2019 consensus recommends MorphMatch in single-chamber devices and SMART in dual-chamber devices/CRT-Ds.
prog-bbm-031.aRetenir: Biotronik: MorphMatch (morphology, single-chamber) or SMART (A/V relationship, multi-chamber), never both, and never in the VF zone.

prog-bbm-032.question: With SMART Detection (Biotronik), when an R-R interval in the VT zone is classified as supraventricular in origin, the VT counter is not simply frozen: it is decremented (by 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 4 depending on the case).
options: True
False
commentaires: Correct: a ventricular cycle increments the counter by 1, and a supraventricular cycle decrements it by 0.25 to 4 depending on the branch.
Incorrect: the counter is not frozen; this up/down counting gradually moves the ICD away from the threshold during a prolonged SVT.
prog-bbm-032.explication: The SMART algorithm classifies each R-R interval in the VT zone as ventricular or supraventricular. An interval of ventricular origin increments the VT counter by 1; an interval of atrial origin decrements it by 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 4 depending on the branch of the decision tree. This "up/down" counting explains why a prolonged SVT gradually moves the ICD away from the detection threshold, whereas a clear-cut VT reaches it quickly. The preset SMART values are 20% for onset and 12% for stability. Understanding this counter helps when analysing an episode in which therapy was delayed or withheld.
prog-bbm-032.aRetenir: SMART: +1 for a ventricular cycle, decrement (0.25 to 4) for a supraventricular cycle.

prog-bbm-033.question: According to the Biotronik implementation of the 2019 ICD programming consensus update, which detection programming is suggested in a patient with no history of VT?
options: VF: 8/12 intervals at 200 bpm; VT: 16 intervals at 150 bpm with ATP
VF ≥ 250 bpm (5 s), VT ≥ 185 bpm (12 s), optional VT-1 monitor zone
VF > 255 bpm, fast VT 230 bpm, VT 185 bpm (20 or 30 cycles + 6/8 majority)
VF 231 bpm (30/40 or 24/30), VT2 188 bpm (30 intervals), VT1 monitor
commentaires: Incorrect: short detection at a low rate is the conventional programming that the consensus aims to avoid.
Incorrect: 250 bpm (5 s) and 185 bpm (12 s) are the settings of the Boston Scientific implementation.
Incorrect: 255 bpm, 230 bpm and the 6/8 majority are the settings of the MicroPort implementation.
Correct: VF 231 bpm with 30/40 (otherwise 24/30), VT2 188 bpm with 30 intervals, VT1 as an optional monitor zone.
prog-bbm-033.explication: The Biotronik appendix of the 2019 update suggests, with no history of VT: VF at 231 bpm with 30/40 intervals if programmable (otherwise 24/30), VT2 at 188 bpm with 30 intervals, and VT1 as an optional monitor zone. VF therapy comprises ATP One Shot (1 burst of 8 pulses at 88% of the cycle length) followed by full-energy shocks. For discriminators: MorphMatch in single-chamber devices, SMART in dual-chamber devices/CRT-Ds, Home Monitoring enabled. For dual-chamber pacing, the appendix suggests DDD with IRS Plus (± CLS) or DDD with Vp Suppression. Each manufacturer has its own implementation (in seconds for Boston Scientific, in cycles with a 6/8 majority for MicroPort). Prolonging detection and raising rate cut-offs reduces inappropriate therapies without increasing mortality, as shown by MADIT-RIT and subsequent studies.
prog-bbm-033.aRetenir: Biotronik 2019: VF 231 bpm (30/40), VT2 188 bpm (30 intervals), VT1 monitor zone.

prog-bbm-034.question: With Biotronik Home Monitoring, the daily data transmission only takes place if the patient manually triggers it from the transmitter.
options: True
False
commentaires: Incorrect: the daily transmission is automatic; the patient does not need to trigger anything.
Correct: the device sends its data automatically every day to the CardioMessenger transmitter, with no action required from the patient.
prog-bbm-034.explication: This is false. Home Monitoring relies on an automatic daily transmission from the device to the transmitter (CardioMessenger), which relays the data to the secure platform reviewed by the team. It transmits, among other things, ongoing arrhythmias, thresholds, sensing amplitudes and impedances, pacing statistics and EGMs. Event-triggered messages complement the daily transmission. The patient has nothing to do, provided the transmitter is plugged in and placed close enough. Remote monitoring does not replace a clinic visit in the event of new symptoms.
prog-bbm-034.aRetenir: Home Monitoring = automatic daily transmission, with no patient involvement.
